name: number-field
pattern: A headless number field adding PageUp/PageDown and cancelable change events to native input[type=number]
responsibility: Preserves native number value, min, max, step, arrow keys, typing, and form semantics. Adds PageUp/PageDown, user-originated change events, data-state, and semantic markup validation that native input lacks. Does not generate appearance or content.

authorMarkup.label: The consumer provides an accessible name through <label>, aria-label, or aria-labelledby.
authorMarkup.range: The consumer supplies min, max, step, and value as native attributes.
authorMarkup.form: The consumer supplies name and uses native number-input form submission.
authorMarkup.content: The controller does not generate elements or content.

semanticElements: The root must be an HTMLInputElement with type=number.
pageStep must be a positive integer.
contractValidation.invalidMarkup: Validate root and configuration on connection. Invalid markup prevents listeners, state output, keyboard handling, and value operations and issues console.warn once per connection. Do not throw.
contractValidation.warning: Use the standard English disabling warning, including a native input[type=number] root and a positive integer pageStep.

pageStep.description: Number of native steps moved by one PageUp/PageDown operation; a positive integer.

value.description: Current native input.valueAsNumber, or NaN for nonnumeric input. Assignment changes value and data-state without custom events.

number-field:beforechange.when: Before trusted pointer/keyboard changes: native change from typing, arrows, or the spinner, and controller-committed PageUp/PageDown
number-field:beforechange.effect: On preventDefault(), restore the previous native value and data-state and suppress number-field:change.

number-field:change.when: After a trusted value change is committed

events.pageKeys: The controller commits PageUp/PageDown with reason keyboard.
events.wheel: Chromium wheel changes cannot be tracked as pending through pointerdown/keydown, so they synchronize state output without custom events. See docs/notes/browser-engine-differences.md.
events.programmatic: The value setter, initialization, form reset, and reconnection do not emit custom events.
events.sameValue: Do not emit beforechange/change when the value has not changed.
events.synthetic: input/change with isTrusted=false only synchronize native value and state outputs; they do not emit custom events. The controller does not dispatch synthetic native input/change events.

consumerIntegration.stimulusActions: Listen for number-field:change and number-field:beforechange on the root or an ancestor. The controller does not stop propagation.
consumerIntegration.cancelableHook: Cancel a change by calling event.preventDefault() in a number-field:beforechange listener.
consumerIntegration.programmatic: Other controllers may read/write value through a Stimulus controller reference or outlets. Programmatic API changes emit no events.
consumerIntegration.nested: Use :self or event.target === event.currentTarget to restrict events to the root when listening outside nested number-field controllers.

behavior.scope: Use one native input[type=number] as the root; there are no targets.
behavior.initial: The native value attribute determines the initial value; the controller has no separate initial value.
behavior.native: Delegate typing, arrows, spinner, wheel, and form semantics to the browser. The controller neither validates nor corrects native values.
behavior.disabled: Do not handle PageUp/PageDown when native input.disabled is true. Do not add disabled data-* attributes. Public API changes remain allowed regardless of disabled state.
behavior.readonly: Do not handle PageUp/PageDown when native input.readOnly is true, matching native arrow keys not changing readonly values.

keyboard.pageUp: Increase by pageStep native steps using stepUp(pageStep); delegate min/max clamping and numeric-error handling to the browser. Use preventDefault to suppress page scrolling.
keyboard.pageDown: Decrease through stepDown(pageStep), following the same rules as pageUp.
keyboard.stepAny: For step="any", stepUp/stepDown throw InvalidStateError in all three measured engines. Use an effective step of one, compute value +/- pageStep, and clamp to min/max, matching the implied step of one used by native arrow keys.
keyboard.homeEnd: Do not implement Home/End. Chromium moves the caret even on macOS (see docs/notes/browser-engine-differences.md), and Windows text fields conventionally use these keys for caret movement. Intercepting them would break editing. APG Spinbutton Home/End guidance assumes a custom widget, not an editable native input; this deviation is intentional.
keyboard.arrows: Leave arrow-key handling entirely to the browser.

managedMarkup.nativeSemantics: Use the native input[type=number] implicit spinbutton role, value, min, max, step, keyboard handling, and form semantics.
managedMarkup.aria: Do not write role, aria-valuenow, aria-valuemin, aria-valuemax, or aria-valuetext. HTML-AAM maps input[type=number] to spinbutton; Chromium measurements show native attributes automatically exposed as value/valuemin/valuemax/valuetext in the accessibility tree. Preserve authored aria-valuetext.
managedMarkup.stateOnly: Only root data-state is controller-managed output. Do not output a CSS custom property: the number is displayed as text and no CSS value consumer is required.
managedMarkup.preservation: Preserve authored id, name, value, min, max, step, disabled, ARIA, and other attributes.

stateOutputs.ownership: Only root data-state is controller-owned; do not use ARIA as a visual state output.
stateOutputs.min: data-state="min" when value equals min. This state cannot occur without min.
stateOutputs.max: data-state="max" when value equals max. This state cannot occur without max.
stateOutputs.between: data-state="between" otherwise, including nonnumeric values such as empty input or badInput.

lifecycle: Register root keydown, input, and change listeners and associated-form reset in connect(); remove them in disconnect().
Synchronize state output from the current native value on reconnection.
Do not duplicate listeners or custom events when reconnecting the same instance

observations.environment: Firefox, WebKit, and screen readers on real devices
observations.item: Accessibility-tree value exposure and number-input announcements
observations.impact: Native number input semantics and validation remain authoritative; the controller does not select alternative ARIA from announcement wording.

acceptanceCriteria: Required AAA criteria: 2.1.3 Keyboard (No Exception), with no pointer-only features; and 3.2.5 Change on Request, with controller focus movement limited to user actions or consumer JS calls, never timers.
The behavior and accessibility implemented by this component must meet WCAG 2.2 Level AA.
Conforming input[type=number] preserves native value, min, max, step, typing, arrow keys, and form semantics.
PageUp/PageDown move by pageStep steps, stop at min/max, and suppress page scrolling.
Home/End remain native caret operations, intentionally differing from the APG Spinbutton Pattern; measurements are recorded in docs/notes/browser-engine-differences.md.
Only trusted value changes emit one cancelable beforechange followed by one committed change, in that order. Cancellation preserves value and state.
Public API calls, initialization, form reset, and reconnection synchronize state outputs without custom events.
The controller adds neither role nor aria-value attributes and preserves authored attributes.
Invalid markup disables enhancement with one warning
Pass automated tests in Chromium, Firefox, and WebKit.
Engine differences in badInput display and wheel value changes are recorded in docs/notes/browser-engine-differences.md.
Report Firefox/WebKit accessibility-tree value exposure and real-device screen reader announcements as unverified.

testMatrix.description: data-state min/max/between, missing bounds, nonnumeric values, and authored-attribute preservation
PageUp/PageDown delegation to stepUp/stepDown, pageStep, effective step one for step="any", min/max clamping, preventDefault, and disabled/readonly no-ops
beforechange cancellation and restoration; change detail, order, and bubbling
Capturing trusted native change from typing/arrows, converting to custom events, and determining reason
No events from value assignment or synthetic input/change, with state synchronization
One warning and disabled enhancement for invalid roots or pageStep

testMatrix: Home/End left to native behavior (covered by number-field-page-keys)
Engine-specific results for Chromium, Firefox, and WebKit
Screen-reader results on a real device (unverified)
